A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CATE evaluation study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original evaluations of 16 models on 43,200 sampled variants from 12 RCT datasets. Appendix D also reports semi-synthetic validation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and simulation results and adds statistical findings in Section 4.2 and bootstrap uncertainty estimates in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The Q and Q-hat evaluation framework, control-variate variants, observational sampling procedure, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Moving the consistency theorem does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 RCT datasets and Hillstrom-based semi-synthetic validation scenarios. v2 clarifies that 43,200 datasets are sampled variants of those 12 sources; it does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain the same 16 CATE models. The zero-effect and constant-effect comparisons, and the evaluation criteria compared in Figure 1 and Appendix D, are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The training-size grid, treatment proportions, assignment-mechanism depths, disjoint estimation/evaluation samples, and Q-hat evaluation criterion remain unchanged. The added bootstrap uncertainty reporting does not revise the underlying benchmark design.

E4.justification: The oracle-ranking simulations and sensitivity analyses for training size, treatment imbalance, and assignment complexity are unchanged. Dataset-level analyses move from Appendix H to I. The added statistical summaries introduce no new ablations or robustness scenarios.

E5.justification: New Appendix H, Table 5, supplies standard errors and 95% confidence intervals for all 16 models' win rates, degeneracy rates, and average ranks using 10,000 bootstrap replications. Section 4.2 also adds significance reporting at the 5% level. This substantially expands empirical uncertainty reporting; the existing 100 sampling repetitions per setting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1's point estimates and the existing plots are unchanged. v2 newly reports that 94% of degenerate estimates differ significantly from zero and adds numerical uncertainty bounds, such as the s.xgb.cv win-rate interval of 0.251–0.259 around the retained estimate of 0.255.

T1.justification: v1's consistency Theorem 3.4 becomes Theorem B.2 in v2, retaining its assumptions, statement, and proof. The remaining definitions, generalization results, control-variate propositions, and convergence argument are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central 62%, 80%, and 30% findings and three contributions remain. However, v2's conclusion adds a broader claim of evaluating real-world heterogeneity without counterfactual ground truth 'for the first time'; v1's explicit priority claim concerned oracle-ranking guarantees under general conditions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds hypotheses connecting orthogonality-based models' underperformance to data generation, modeling choices, and assumption violations. The conclusion newly emphasizes the benchmark's preliminary scope, missing high-sample evidence, and the distinction between inadequate evaluation practices and stalled methodological progress.

D1.justification: Appendices C–F retain the same model implementations, preprocessing, propensity clipping, and data-generation instructions. Software references and the commitment to release code after approval are unchanged. The bootstrap count adds statistical reporting, without new implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Positioning receives limited revisions: Section 2.2 changes the criticism that simulation 'zeroes out' real-world heterogeneity to 'misrepresents' it, and the conclusion introduces broader priority wording for the proposed evaluation approach.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title, affiliation, abstract, and introductory wording, rewrites the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments. It relocates the consistency theorem and inserts Appendix H, renaming the former H as I. These are localized revisions within the retained document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 with uncertainty columns, adjusts existing table typography and spacing, and shortens Figure 1's caption. Existing plots retain their content; other visual differences largely reflect local reflow and appendix relabeling.

improvement.justification: The bootstrap intervals in Appendix H and clearer distinction between 12 source datasets and 43,200 sampled variants improve transparency and interpretation. The gains are limited: the bootstrap resampling unit and degeneracy-test procedure remain unspecified, while broader novelty and 'all learners are weak' wording exceeds the earlier, more precise framing without additional benchmark evidence.
